reason: E1 supports that 20 wt.% WC particles improve hardness and wear resistance in a HEA matrix, but the hypothesis extends this to a TiAl matrix without direct evidence. E2 mentions laser cladding of coatings on Ti6Al4V and reinforcement of TiAl alloys, but not specifically a TiAl+WC composite. No cited evidence addresses metallurgical compatibility, uniform WC distribution, or preservation of TC4's lightweight and corrosion resistance.
premises: Adding ~20 wt.% WC particles to a metallic matrix increases hardness and wear resistance
Laser surface cladding can produce a TiAl-based composite coating on Ti6Al4V
A TiAl matrix coating is metallurgically compatible with TC4 and provides solid-solution strengthening
WC particles in the coating will be uniformly distributed and impede dislocation motion
The coating will not degrade TC4's lightweight and corrosion-resistant characteristics
